name: Entity reference list (SYNTHETIC)
access: Fixture file in fixtures/demo. Stands in for a reference table built from public company and facility registries. No live equivalent is implemented yet.
licensing: All names and identifiers are fictional. No license applies.
update_cadence: Static fixture. A real registry feed would change slowly.
matching_limitations: Assumes this list is complete. Real registries have duplicate names across jurisdictions, which the resolver must handle.

name: Supplier disclosures (SYNTHETIC)
access: Fixture file in fixtures/demo. Stands in for buyer-published supplier lists.
licensing: Fictional data. Real supplier lists vary by publisher and may restrict reuse.
update_cadence: Static fixture. Real disclosures are usually refreshed annually or quarterly.
matching_limitations: Often names suppliers without registry IDs, so matches rely on name and state and can be ambiguous.

name: Facility registry (SYNTHETIC)
access: Fixture file in fixtures/demo. Stands in for a public operator-to-facility registry.
update_cadence: Static fixture. Real facility registries update irregularly.
matching_limitations: Operator-to-facility links may be incomplete. A missing link does not prove there is no relationship.

name: Regulatory notices (SYNTHETIC)
access: Fixture file in fixtures/demo. Stands in for government notices that name a facility or company.
update_cadence: Static fixture. Real notice feeds are typically updated daily.
matching_limitations: Notices often name companies informally. Records that name a company without a state or registry ID are not linked.

name: Trade news (SYNTHETIC)
access: Fixture file in fixtures/demo. Stands in for news articles.
licensing: Fictional data. Real news content is copyrighted and must not be stored without a license.
update_cadence: Static fixture. Real news is continuous.
matching_limitations: Two companies appearing in one article is only a co-mention. It is not evidence of a business relationship, so Blindspot never uses co-mentions for discovery.
